title: postmortem-driven-release-throttle-with-operator-latch
author: Anika Shah
release_notes: Add postmortem-driven release throttle and an operator latch to allow manual intervention during automated rollouts. Enables tighter incident-to-rollout feedback and safe overrides for urgent responses.
body:
Motivation: After several incident postmortems we observed that automatic rollouts often kept progressing past the earliest signals that correlated with recent incidents (high tail latency, error spikes tagged in our incident system). This PR adds a release throttle that integrates postmortem/incident signals into rollout controllers and an operator latch that lets on-call or release engineers hold/resume promotions without taking the full release offline.

Summary: Implements a Postmortem-Driven Release Throttle (PDRT) and Operator Latch. PDRT consumes a compact incident summary feed (severity, tags, implicated services, confidence) from the incident service (SUP pipeline). When a relevant incident is active or within a configured cooldown window, the throttle reduces commit velocity of canary/A-B/staged rollouts by applying a soft cap to promotion percentage and enforcing additional smoke validation checkpoints. The Operator Latch is an override mechanism visible in Console and CLI that allows authorized users to: (1) force-hold a rollout, (2) force-resume with audit comment, or (3) enable temporary fast-path for emergency fixes. Audit logs and KMS-backed signatures are recorded for all latch actions.

What changed (high-level):
- rollout/controller: add PDRT integration point, incident consumer, and throttle policy evaluation.
- orchestration/api: expose latch endpoint (POST /rollouts/:id/latch) with RBAC checks and audit recording.
- console/ui: add a compact latch control and incident context summary on rollout details page.
- telemetry: new rollout_throttle.{applied,reason} metrics and histograms for throttle_fraction.
- rollout-playbooks: default canary manifest updated to include incident_cooldown and soft_throttle settings.

Design notes:
- The incident consumer is intentionally compact and defensive: it only considers incidents with scope:inference, tags intersecting ["latency", "timeout", "model-serving"], and severity >= P2. Default cooldown is 2h after incident resolution.
- Throttle is a soft policy: it scales down target traffic fraction according to severity-weighted budget. Example: severity P1 -> cap 10% per 15m increment, P2 -> cap 30%, P3 -> no cap.
- Operator latch is independent of PDRT. Users with release:manage or sre:respond roles can act. All actions record an audit entry and create a telemetry event for retrospective analysis.

Rollout behavior examples: (embedded in the controller logic)
1) Canary started at 1%. Simultaneous P1 incident detected that matches model-serving tags -> throttle applies cap to 10% and pauses auto-escalation beyond that until additional smoke checks pass or incident cooldown ends.
2) A/B experiment: throttle will rebalance incremental allocations to new variant conservatively while preserving minimum retention for control.
3) Shadow seeding unaffected but sampling rate is reduced if incident indicates saturation on GPU nodes.

Security & compliance: Latch endpoints require RBAC and audit trails. Audit entries are forwarded to the existing audit-log-exporter pipeline. We added KMS signature stamps for manual overrides to prove operator intent for postmortem timelines.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests: controller policy evaluation, incident filter heuristics, latch RBAC.
- Integration tests: simulated incident feed via test harness that asserts throttle_fraction metrics, rollback triggers, and latch audit entries.
- E2E: staged canary in perf-canary cluster with synthetic incident generator used to validate soft-throttle behavior and safe resume paths.
- Load test: ensure telemetry tag cardinality remains bounded when many incidents correlate.

Commits: ["feat(controller): add postmortem throttle policy and evaluation", "feat(api): latch endpoints + RBAC enforcement", "ui: add latch button and incident context panel", "chore(tests): add integration tests for incident feed", "docs: rollout playbook and operator guide"]

notes_for_release: Behind feature flag release.postmortem_throttle; rollout plan: internal 0% -> 10% after 48h -> 50% after 7d with SRE sign-off. Operator guide and playbook added under docs/operator/release-latch.md.
post_merge_observations: Initial rollout to 0% observed expected telemetry events. Integration test harness recorded throttle_fraction histogram buckets consistent with simulated severity weights. No regressions in canary pipeline. One minor UI accessibility note fixed in follow-up PR.
changelog_entry: Add postmortem-driven soft throttle and operator latch for controlled rollouts. Improves safety of automated promotions during incident windows.
